representative_tasks.task: Validation accuracy is noisy and low; the loop is wrapped in torch.no_grad() - is model.eval() still needed?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Explains no_grad only disables autograd; model.eval() switches Dropout off and BatchNorm to running statistics; pairs eval() with train() before training resumes

representative_tasks.task: torch.save(model) every epoch, overwriting the file - is that enough to resume after a crash?
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Saves a dict of model/optimizer state_dicts plus epoch (and scheduler/scaler state), writes atomically via a temp file and os.replace, loads with weights_only=True and resumes at epoch + 1

representative_tasks.task: Write a custom Dataset/DataLoader and train/eval loop for tabular data
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Dataset doing per-sample work with a length check, DataLoader handling batching/shuffling, a loop that zeroes grads every batch and switches train/eval modes

negative_cases: DataLoader(num_workers>0) on Windows without an if __name__ == '__main__' guard (planned)
Forward hook registered for feature extraction but never removed (planned)
rubric: Distinguishes autograd control (no_grad/inference_mode) from layer mode (train/eval)
Checkpoints state_dicts (model, optimizer, epoch, scheduler/scaler) rather than pickled modules
Loads checkpoints with weights_only=True and does not recommend weights_only=False for untrusted files
Atomic checkpoint writes so a crash mid-save cannot corrupt the only checkpoint
prerequisites: example-deps (torch, numpy) for executable tests; CPU only
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md) and run via run_evals.py --run-executable; they run CPU-only.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: A trained MLP whose evaluate() leaves it in eval mode
A checkpoint file written atomically (no .tmp left after success or a failed save) that restores identical weights and resumes at epoch + 1
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
Executable tests run CPU-only; CUDA-specific behaviour (pin_memory, device placement on GPU) is not exercised.
The executable tests prove the skill's checkpoint code round-trips and survives a simulated crash mid-write; they do not prove a response wrote equivalent code.

An independent reviewer's stress test (30 texts written after reading the patterns, so adversarial rather than blind; 23 wrong, 7 correct across all five skills of this workstream) initially had 16/23 wrong answers passing every hard assertion and 6/7 correct answers failing one. The patterns were then fixed and these texts kept verbatim as fail.adversarial* / pass.blind* fixtures, so the post-fix 30/30 is a regression result, not a held-out discrimination rate.
unsupported_use_cases: Mixed precision, LR schedules, early stopping (training-deep-models)
Threat analysis of loading untrusted pickles from third parties (ai-ml-security)
